title: 3.1x3.1x1.1 inches, big heavy powerful charger, UL Listed for electrical safety
text:
I hesitated to order this charger after reading several news reports about the electrical safety of AmazonBasics products. I am very happy to see that this charger is UL Listed, which should indicate that it has been tested for safety by an independent laboratory. For safety reasons, many US companies will only buy electrical devices that are UL Listed or UL Certified.

GaN chargers are advertised as being more efficient and compact than silicon chargers. At 3.1x3.1x1.1 inches, this is the biggest heaviest wall charger that I have seen. Make sure your wall outlet is sturdy enough to hold it.

The power rating is 60-100W for the first USB-C port, 18W for the 2nd USB-C port, and 12W each for the 2 USB-A ports. I don't have any devices that draw more than 60W, but I assume the charger will only deliver the 100W to the USB-C port if none of the other ports are being used. The charger does run cool and quiet no matter what I have plugged in to it.

There are no USB-C cables in the box with the charger. For safety reasons, you should use only a high quality cable with chargers rated 15W or higher. Most companies are including a high-power cable (with thicker or extra wires in the casing) with their chargers to make sure customers use a safe combination.

title: Almost perfect.
text:
This charger is almost perfect for me. It's everything you'd expect in a wireless phone charger. It uses a USB to USB-C adapter. It's large, stable, and has three small feet to keep it from sliding around. It's thin. It charges quickly. It's effective through a case. I have this charger in black and white and it looks great in both colors.

Complaints, it comes with a silicone 'case' that wraps around the outside. The problem with the device is that the silicone sleeve should have been part of the device and not in addition to. It doesn't stay in place well if the device gets slid around. I've got small children who do things one wouldn't expect, the charge gets moved, the sleeve slides up and needs to be readjusted. I initially place the charger on an end table with a thick cloth covering it. The charger was at a slight angle because of this and without the sleeve, the phone with and without a case slowly slid off until it was no longer charging. The charger looks better without and I like the glossy look, but adding something grippy to the surface would have been a great design choice.

The Anker charger, which I also have, has a matte surface with a slightly grippier texture that works better but looks worse. I wish this device found a middle road. If you have a silicone case, it would probably be perfect without the sleeve. And if you do not have kids, the sleeve may not be an issue.

It's just that in my particular set of circumstances, it's so close to hitting all the right marks.

title: Bound To Protect While Bound To Annoy The Eagle Eyed
text:
This case protects my iPhone 5S very well. I have no issues with that at all. The case is raised a tad above the screen so you can lay it face down on a table. It completely covers the power button and volume buttons. It does not cover the silent switch or anything on the bottom of the phone.

The photo looks like it's hard plastic but it's actually more of a hard rubber. Think the kind of thick rubber you'd find under a car floor mat. The sides are an even harder plastic. These hard sides make it virtually impossible not to touch the side of your phone while putting the case on. Both my finger and fingernails banged up against the side of my phone a few times while putting it on, but I didn't see any scuffs. Because the hard plastic sides grab so tightly around the edge of your phone, I have a hard time seeing how any dirt will get in, even at holes for the silent switch and from the bottom.

With that being said....

I have a difficult time pressing the power button with my hand in front of the phone. I can feel I'm fighting with the hard single piece of plastic top edge. It can be pressed, it just takes that extra bit of pressure. If I use a finger of the hand holding the phone from the back, with my finger reaching up from behind and pressing the top - it's quiet easy from that direction.

While the volume buttons are easy to press from any angle, the silent switch is fairly recessed and I really have to line up the narrowest point on my fingernail with it and wedge it in there some to use it. It only takes a second, but still feels longer than it took with my hard plastic iPhone 4S case.

On the bottom, while there is no hard plastic bottom side, there is a thin soft rubber edge on the front side of the phone. It droops ever so slightly. It also bumps right up to my earphone port so earphones with a larger jack may have issues. I pushed mind hard into it, it mushed the plastic a bit but the earphones went in and have not come out, even while in a car holder.

In third place for a negative issue I have is that the cases rubber outline takes away from the beauty of the phone. I know I'm asking for the impossible - a case that can protect while also retaining the original look and feel of the phone. But the hard plastic case I had for my 4S really kept the look better than this case does for the 5s. The rubber along the edges is just a tad too pronounced and, well, rubber looking. I no longer see the beautiful mirror-shiney gold edges. The back of my phone looks nice though, even though this is a "Frosted" back. I would have preferred perfectly clear, but oh well.

The runner-up worst issue is that the case comes up high enough over the screen that my fingers constantly bump against is when swiping horizontally. Like swiping back on Safari, or iMessage, or Mail. I'm learning that my finger doesn't need to start that far onto the edge for these features to work though, so perhaps I just need to get used to that.

The worst, for someone like me with an eagle eye, is that I see imperfections in the plastic. On the top a bit to the left there is what I thought was a tiny hair. But it's just a little knick in the rubber, or maybe a seam of some kind. On the back there are specs of what looks like dust between my phone and the case but when I removed the case to look, I saw the dirt specs were inside the rubber of the case. So I will forever see these bits that I want to wipe away but can't.

Now...

While the bad is written out longer than the good, that's because it takes more to explain the bad. I still like this case. Especially for the cheap price. I know this case will protect my phone well, and thats really my main concern. I can always buy another case if I so choose. It would be much more difficult and expensive to get a new phone. So I will continue to use this case and see if my feelings change.

PS: I use this with the Tech Armor screen protector and the case does not effect the screen protector at all. Ending on a positive note, woo!

title: Disappointing Application
text:
Phone I installed this on: iPhone XS

Super disappointed. Didn’t realize there would be an actual black edge printed into the screen protector. Who does that??? The picture of the listing makes it look like the black edge is just for the sake of the photo. But it’s not. So if you don’t install it absolutely perfectly, the black edge will cover a small portion of your phone screen. I was off my one millimeter and now the bezel in the left side of my screen is superficially wider than the right side. It’s not noticeable to most, but I definitely notice it.
This was not an easy to install for me, and I’ve done this many times. So it will be not be the easiest for newbies because the instructions are not detailed at all.
The product comes with a “wet wipe” which I thought was alcohol but it did such a terrible job of removing smudges on my phone screen, so I used real rubbing alcohol from my medicine cabinet. The “drying wipe” left so much lint on the screen. The “dust removing” stickers were not even sticky at ALL. Dust just got picked up and moved to another part of the screen as I moved it around. It also comes with “guiding stickers”, but the instructions do not give you any information on how to use them. But, I used them before from another screen protector so I knew what it was for. You don’t need the guiding stickers at all for this specific screen protector though. Just line up the hole at the top with your phone and slowly press down and out. I was able to line it up fine, but to my horror a piece of lint was missed and now I have a bubble on the middle of my screen. Infuriating!
I gave this product 2 stars (instead of 1) because I think the glass screen protector itself is not bad. It truly is oleophobic, because I see that it attracts way less fingerprints than my last screen protector. It also protects to the edges of my screen and responds really well to touch, which was something my last one didn’t do.
If this came with no black border, better instructions, and better wipes & stickers, it could easily be a 5-star product. Too bad it doesn’t.

title: Good everyday use iPhone case for basic protection
text:
This was a last minute purchase. I bought this case because this was the only one available for delivery on the day my iPhone 7 plus was to arrive. I was a little skeptical given the number of user reviews, but am pleasantly surprised by how functional this product is.

I don't drop my phone a lot, nor do I have kids or pets in my house. So the primary purpose of buying this case was to protect my phone from dirt, minor spills and scratches from everyday use.

It's a clear, transparent case, rubberized, but not supple. It's hard enough to provide a solid cover for the phone. It was easy to slip my phone into the case, and the case fit it perfectly. Pretty snug, not bulky at all.

It also has tiny, raised button-like features over the power button (left) and the volume controls (right). They perfectly coincide with the phone's buttons; also they are sensitive to touch, so you don't have to press down too hard to use these features. There's an opening on the back for the camera and on the side for the mute button; also perfectly positioned.

It think it's a good case for users who aren't looking for heavy-duty protection. Provides good, basic cover for the phone w/o taking away from the design of the phone. I can still see all the accents on the side of the phone and apple logo on the back; it''s a good look.

title: Very nice small wireless charger
text:
This is a nice small wireless charger. It's very thin and comes with a rubber ring that gives it and grip when it sits on your desk. The connection is USB type-c which is nice. The 10-watt power rating means it's fairly safe for both phones that can take a wireless charge. It also means it's not going to be the fastest charger but if you're using a wireless charger you're probably not concerned about that.

The surface of it is very glossy and does pick up fingerprints very easily. It comes with what looks like a 3 foot USB type-c cable which is likely too short to be a actual use for most people. But it's nice to think or to the cable. there is no power brick so you'll need to supply your own AC adapter.

I had no problems charging my Galaxy S10e with this charger. I do prefer the look of the Amazon wireless charger to my seneo charger as it looks sleeker and more refined. The only thing I would change is to make the surface a little less prone to fingerprints.

title: It's not just a TPU skin - it has a hard back. A good choice for the money.
text:
I almost considered getting Speck’s clear iPhone 7 case until I saw the Amazon Basics one for so much less. Sometimes you just want to go naked with you phone, and this case fits the bill without going all the way.

This case consists of two components – a hard polycarbonate back piece with a softer TPU bumper. Each corner has an air bubble imbedded in the case for cushioning in case of a corner drop. All of the buttons are covered and the cutouts for the camera and the ring/silent switch are perfect. The speaker and mic cutouts on the bottom are in alignment and the lightning connector cutout should work for most cables and headphones. The bumper gives a better grip than the iPhone itself, but some might find it a little bit slick. Personally I think its fine, better than my previous Moshi iPhone 6 case was. There is also a nice lip around the display, so if the phone is put face down it is not touching the surface.

At a quick glance my matte iPhone 7 looks like a Jet Black model from the back, then you realize it is the case that is glossy and not the phone. The matte black finish will not give the liquid look like the jet black does in this case like some of the reviewer’s pictures show. The case does seem to attract some fingerprints, so to keep it looking clean it occasionally needs to be cleaned off.

Because this has a hard back and it just not a “skin” like a lot of the flexible TPU cases out there on Amazon are, the Amazon Basics clear case for iPhone 7 is a better choice for the money and will offer better protection. I just hope that it doesn’t yellow like most of the clear cases do, but only time will tell that.

title: The best case for your iPhone 5!
text:
For my needs this is the absolute best case you can get for your iPhone 5. It's amazing that this case is so good considering that it is probably the least expensive case you will consider.

Don't be fooled by the price! This is a quality product that completely protects your phone from scratches and yet keeps it slim enough to easily fit in your pocket.

The case is made from a semi-ridgid gel-like material. It is not "sticky" like a rubber cover and will easily slide into your pocket without catching but yet it is also soft enough to provide a very small amount of cushioning to the phone (compared to hard plastic cases). The softer material also makes it easier to install or remove the case from your phone.

This case completely surrounds the sides and back of the phone, and even has a slight edge to it that "rolls over" onto the front of the phone. This makes sure that the sides are completely protected but it also adds just a tiny amount of space to the front of the phone which allows you to place the phone face down on a table without the actual screen of the phone touching the surface of the table.

There are cutouts for the silent switch, the camera on the back, and the headphone/microphones/speakers/charging port on the bottom. The volume buttons and top screen on/off button are duplicated as buttons on the case so the actual buttons are not exposed.

This case also includes an optional plastic sticky screen protector film that you can use if you are concerned about the screen itself getting scratched.

All in all this is hands down my favorite iPhone 5 case and the one I recommend to friends. It does exactly what I want without adding much bulk and comes in at a fantastic price from Amazon.

title: Awkward & poorly designed, though quite strong & aesthetic
text:
The 2-material (strong + fluffy) AmazonBasics PC/Silicon Case for iPhone 5 has not only all the benefits of the concept, but also all the disadvantages of the innovative, though flawed design, that exceed the benefits. The polycarbonate (PC) shell swaddles and provides strength to the fluffy and shock absorbing silicon core, but the thick case sticks up too high next to the screen edge that makes it very difficult, if not impossible for some, to touch the screen next to the edge using the thumb. In cases where only silicon turns up and is close the the screen edges the pressing thumbs can compress the soft silicon and this difficulty is not as pronounced. However, AmazonBasics has also the hard PC shell turned up that prevents squeezing the silicon. If the hard PC shell was turned up along the shorter sides of the case, instead of the longer, that problem would not exist.

Otherwise, the case is good. It is lightweight, rounded as without edges, fits perfectly, not slippery, does not cover anything requiring direct access including controls and dock connector allowing charging while in case, has very functional protrusions covering the buttons and allowing to feel and press them as without the cover. The surface is smooth and does not attract grime, though it can be easily washed in the unlikely event. It seems inferior to more expensive luxurious Spigen cases and similarly priced Belkin Shield cases, which also have simplistic cutouts for the buttons instead of the covering protrusions covering the buttons and allowing to feel and press them as without the cover.

title: So far, so good.
text:
I have a terrible track record with headphones, not because they were bad per se, but because I'm very rough with, and don't take very good care of them. They usually get tangled to no end, rolled over on, slept on, etc.. and sooner rather than later they die, do my own lack of care.

This is my latest pair, and 1st of this brand, and so far they are holing up pretty well. The sound quality is clear and good enough for my needs, and the headphones themselves seem durable. They still tangle a bit at times, but no where near as often as past pairs, and when the do, they are easily untangled, due to the material.

My favorite thing about this pair, are the earbud covers. Unlike past pairs, these don't come off and leave me having to struggle to put them back on. The most that has happened is that they have flipped upward but still remain secure in their place, so I just have to adjust them downward when this happens. In the past I would struggle to put them back on and in other instances, they just get lost overtime from coming off and going wherever they go....So far, such is not the case with this pair, and for that I'm thankful.

Happy with this pair so far. Works as expected and seems durable enough.

For about a month the product worked great. Calls came in clear and no one reported any trouble hearing me. The Remote Button paused and played my podcasts as great as I could have hoped.

Then about a month after buying it I noticed that it was hard to hear what I was listening to if there was any noise around me whatsoever, even when I turned up the volume all the way. At first I thought it was just the file, but I found that if I removed the Adapter, I could hear everything crystal clear and loud.

I tested it on a number of headphones, cheap and expensive, and they all had the same problem while using it.

Maybe I just had a bad unit, but I would not buy this again.

This is an obvious statement but not so easy to achieve if you've used your phone for a few days before installing the cover. Sahara provides a very useful cleaning kit and lint scavenging film - not all manufacturers do. I spend twice as long cleaning and removing lint as I do actually placing the cover, but this extra time pays off by eliminating airspace between the cover an phone screen that reduces touch sensitivity. Well worth the effort, and a good purchase...

The outer rubber case is a very stiff rubber, not at all flimsy.  One concern I had with buying this online was the possibility of getting a fake.  Unfortunately, it looks like all the reviews overlap for products making it hard to determine what review goes with the product from which seller.  I bought mine from Amazon directly.  Other sellers are more likely to be fakes.  If the price seems too low, it probably is a fake, but that doesn't mean fakes can't be priced the same as the real deal.  My advise is to stick with "Ships from and sold by Amazon". Also, look at the Otterbox website for available colors.  If it is a color not available on their website, then it is probably fake.  I am going to try to attach pictures, so you can see the packaging (also an indication of a potential fake).  I would definitely recommend this case!

title: My favorite battery case, ever!
text:
Made of a matte finish black rubber, it feels good in the hand. It doesn't add much girth as compared to what I'm already carrying, and it's anything but slippery. Like all battery cases, it's heavy. And that should be expected since you've just added a battery to your phone that is about 1.5x bigger than the factory battery. But that also means that you can expect that this case will give you about 2.5x the battery life that you are currently accustomed to, in a convenient and easy to carry case.

I love that the case uses a lightning cord to charge. Nothing I hate more than an iPhone accessory that expects me to carry some sort of extra cord just to support it. So there is the convenience of being able to charge and sync with your existing cables and chargers. The case itself has it's own Lightning Port for charging, and it will charge your phone via Qi (the same way it charges your phone on the go) while it charges itself.

The great news about this case is that it leaves your iPhone's Lightning port accessible so you can still use CarPlay, corded headphones, or any other thing that you may want to use your Lightning Port for. And this is the first case that I've ever seen do that. It's such a simple thing that is simply genius.

While the case does use Qi to charge your iPhone X, it doesn't support wireless charging to charge itself. That seems a little silly, at face value, considering out simple it would be to add it. But Qi is slow, as compared to what can be accomplished with a Lightning Port. And there's a lot of battery here that needs to be charged. So Qi might not be able to top off both your battery case and the phone, in an overnight wireless charging scenario.

Expect AT LEAST a 12-hour charge cycle at the end of your day. And if you drained the battery completely, it could go as long as 24-hours to completely recharge both your phone and this battery case. But if you are concerned about getting it all done, you can charge both your phone and your case, at the same time, using two Lightning Cords and an appropriate, high-power charging source.

I've tested and used a great many cases over the years, and this is far, and away, the one I am most excited about. Since my iPhone X is likely to be replaced later this year, I'm hopeful this simple little trick of leaving the Lightning Port uncovered is added to all of their future cases. It's certainly something that I'm going to be demanding from any case that I buy moving forward.

This would be a 5 star product if it weren't for the obvious deception in the title that would no doubt go unnoticed by the uninitiated. The title does state that this is a 15 watt charger which it is, but where the deception comes in is that it states its a "Super Fast Wireless Charger" which it is not. For those that are more tech savvy, would know that a 15 watt charger is only capable of a fast charge, and not capable of the 45 watt Super Fast charge which most modern phones are capable of these days. Now I usually wouldn't remove 2 stars for a deception that is as obvious as this one. However, I did this time because of the position it will put potential buyers in. People don't just purchase chargers that will work for their phone anymore. Many people are looking for a charger that will charge their phone at the fastest rate its capable of, which for most modern premium phones that's the 45 watt super fast charging. So many buyers would see super fast in the tile and purchase this charger only to find out that it wont meet their primary reason for purchasing it which is the super fast charging.

Like I said this would be a 5 star product if it weren't for the deception in the title. I really like the charger. It has amazing quality, and you can tell a fair amount of energy was expended in designing it. Its capable of charging your phone at the 15 watt "fast charging" rate, which is more than adequate for a wireless charger. I charged my phone from 36 percent to full and the phone was just barely warm, which if you have used wireless chargers before you know that many make your phone blazing hot the longer they charge. The charger is cosmetically appealing with its sleek design and padded bottom where the bottom of your phone contacts the charger. When you pick it up it has heft to it and feels solid in the hand. Even the USB-C port on the charger has a solid contact, whereas many foreign made chargers have a flimsy usb connection.

This is one of those times where rating this product kind of hurt my heart, because its such a good product. If they remove the deceptive title and just list it as a "fast wireless charger". I will update my review of this product to 5 stars.

The description was confusing. The phone fits inside the rubber case which interferes a little with the buttons underneath the screen. There is a plastic shell that covers part of the back of the rubber case. The black plastic holster and clip covers the face of the phone. The screen protector is clear, rigid plastic similar to a food container. It is not a piece of film and it has a slightly grainy quality. I thought it was part of the packaging until I read a review here that noted how much they disliked it.

Phone by itself weighs 4.7 ounces
Phone with the rubber case + hard plastic shell weighs 6.9 ounces
Phone with the rubber case + hard plastic shell + hard plastic holster with clip weighs 8.8 ounces

The entire 3-piece contraption adds 1/4 lb to your phone and together weighs more than 1/2 lb.

The package notes that it has been dropped tested to 15+ feet. That means I can open a 2nd story window and drop it to the ground and it should survive. Since the phone with just a thin plastic case was dropped about 3 feet and did not survive the excess bulk is worth lugging around.

text: Dropped my phone and shattered my screen, considered having Batteries+ replace my screen for $110, but the guy said there was a 50/50 chance that the screen will not work right. title: You know you want it
text:
Let me start off by saying that the Apple MFi Certified iPhone Fast Charger is a great product. It comes with a 20W USB C Power Delivery Wall Charger Plug and a 6ft Type C to Lightning Cable, which makes it easy to charge your iPhone or iPad quickly and efficiently.

One thing I really appreciate about this product is that it's Apple MFi Certified, which means it's been tested and approved by Apple to work with their devices. This gives me peace of mind that I'm not damaging my phone or risking my safety by using a non-certified charger.

The 20W charger is powerful enough to charge my phone quickly, even when it's almost dead. The 6ft cable is also a nice touch, as it gives me more freedom to move around while my phone is charging.

Another thing I appreciate about this product is that the cable can also be used for data syncing, which is great if you need to transfer photos or other files from your phone to your computer.

Overall, I highly recommend the Apple MFi Certified iPhone Fast Charger to anyone who needs a reliable and efficient way to charge their iPhone or iPad. It's a bit on the pricey side, but the quality and peace of mind it provides are well worth the investment.

While this seems like a nit, for someone like me that uses their phone a LOT for business, it is extremely annoying.  The phone also performs very poorly on the SPRINT network... Sprint has enough problems with lousy service to begin with but couple this with a phone that has poor network performance and you have a disastrous combination. I generally feel that 2 tin cans and a string would work better.  And last but not least... battery life is pathetic on this phone.  In conclusion... get yourself an HTC!!!  You will be much happier.  I can't wait until I can throw this phone in the trash!!!

title: Great design with nice features
text: This is an awesome case and I can tell Spigen has been improving their designs in the last few years. The last case I had by them was a lightweight plastic case for my Galaxy S4. While it was slim, the biggest flaw was that it had thin parts around the button cutouts which would crack and fall off after a while - creating sharp edges which then had to be sanded down, until I eventually just stopped using the case. This case does not have cut-outs for buttons, but instead has TPU flexible buttons overlaying the device buttons which works quite well. This effectively solves the problem described above and I'm pleased that I won't have to deal with that this time around. The underside of this case is constructed from clear and hard polycarbonate - which looks great if you want the original design to show through, also having slightly raised corners so that it does not get scratched up when you set it down on a table. The air cushions on the corners are a nice feature which has apparently been added because drop impacts to this area has been shown to crack screens more often than in other areas. I've been fortunate enough to have not dropped my Pixel XL yet, but I will be glad I was using this case when that time inevitably comes.

title: Want a Simple Cell Phone for Phone/Text use?  DON'T BUY THIS ONE!
text:
Got this phone from Verizon 2 years ago (August 2012) on my contract. Have been with Verizon for over a decade, but it is getting more and more difficult to get what I guess is termed to be 'an old style phone'. The worst feature of this phone is the 'locking' feature. You can program the phone to require either one key or two keys to lock/unlock. I use two keys, because the one key method is even more useless than the two key method. The two keys used are both 'high' in the key pad landscape and they are right next to each other. You can lock the phone, slip it into your pocket, and it unlocks immediately, quicker than you can unlocked it manually by hitting the two required keys. I don't use the internet on my phone, I had to call Verizon and have them disable my assess to the internet because the phone simply connected itself to the internet in my pocket so often. There are still problems though. Carrying the phone in a pocket or purse it unlocks every time (and always has) and it calls people and finds screens and features that I didn't know existed and can't even find by looking.

Second worst feature; it took me buying multiple tunes for ring tones to use for the alarm feature and for the call ring tones. I like to use different tones for different friends and families and for different alarm features. I kept missing calls and alarms, and my family swore I was just getting hard of hearing. So when I got with my family and some friends, I stood right in front of them, put the phone behind my back, and had them call me. I could faintly hear the phone ringing, because I knew the tone I guess, but each of them during independent trials, would say something like; 'Well, how long does it take to start ringing?'. Of course, I would say 'It is ringing and has been for a few rings'. They had to admit then that they couldn't hear it either. Part of the problem is that the speaker is on the back of the phone and if you lay it on a table it muffles the sound; but turning it over doesn't really help all that much, and I was holding the phone in my hand when testing it with my friends and family. I bought so many tunes trying to find one that played loud enough to hear on the phone, Verizon finally credited me the price for some of them when I explained that I, nor anyone else, could hear them ring on the phone.

The speaker phone works better for having a conversation than trying to hear the person on the other end of the phone. Of course, I don't want to use a speaker phone in public, but I always do at home. It has blue-tooth capability for hands-free use in your car, but of course, it is so far behind the blue-tooth technology in the car, it won't stay synched. But, I wasn't too upset about that; I didn't expect it to have great advanced technology, I just want the phone to be usable as - a phone.

I love that it is multiple alarms with snooze features and variable settings, which I use every day to wake me and to remind me of ebay auctions or desired other reminders. However, finding different ring tones for each of them was a bit of a pain since so many are not audible on this phone.

I know this technology is old and Verizon is trying to make it difficult for customers to find an old-fashioned inexpensive phone (actually the first one I purchased in 2012 and used for four hours was worse than this one, but I can't for the life of me remember what it was-really tried to wipe it from my memory). Keeping it difficult for people who just want phones to use as phones will culminate in more of us buying advanced, expensive phones with features we don't want and with data packages we don't want or need and therefore higher bills from Verizon. But for people who think a phone is for calling and maybe texting (it does have slide-out keyboard which works great), (the texting is something the younger persons in my family require if you want to communicate with them), this is one of the few phones Verizon had available. My entire family has Verizon phone service and they are not inclined to change and frankly, I wouldn't either. Verizon's customer service quality has become a little spotty of late, but there actual phone coverage and service is great! After trying over half of the other companies when looking for business service for a company where I previously was in charge of buying phones and acquiring services, I can attest Verizon provides the best coverage nation-wide, hands down.

But, I am not interested in the newer phones and with using my phone as a computer; I have a desk top, a lap top, and a Kindle. If that isn't enough computer and internet access for me; I need to quit communicating. I don't need a phone when I am out and about to find out where I am going, I am perfectly capable of finding business locations and how to get from A to B without a computer, been doing it for years using my own internal devices. But, I would like to have a dependable, quality phone for making calls, taking a few photos, and texting with a keyboard.

I am thinking 'good luck to me' now as I go out looking for a new phone. I don't know if this Samsung Intensity II is still available from Verizon, but I note there are several available today (09-21-2014) on Amazon; therefore, I am writing this review as there may be individuals considering purchasing one from Amazon. My recommendation? DONT!!! I have been using cells phones for years and this is without question the worst phone (except the one I had for four-hours) I have ever owned and it has caused me to use language I didn't even know I knew.

title: Easy to Install, Excellent Instructions, Great Results
text:
The Mr. Shield glass screen protector is very easy to install and has a great installation instruction video. The installation went flawlessly, with several minor bubbles that disappeared with only a minor wipe with the "bubble remover" card. After using a very highly rated screen protector with very poor results, I returned to Mr Shield, with which I've had good results for past phones.

Note that there is a noticeable margin around the edge of the screen (maybe 1/32") to allow for a case to slightly overlap the front of the phone. This may be the source of the "halo" complaint by many of the reviewers. My Pixel 3 XL phone has a flat face. I can understand why these "glass" screen protectors may not be suitable for phones with curved wrap-around edges, such as the new Samsung phones.

I am very happy with these screen protectors.

title: Highly Recommended!
text: The screen protection this product provides is very reassuring. Though it would be helpful if they went into more detail on what you are placing over your phone screen. So I will, it is a very thin layer of clear plastic made of whatever it is. The process involves three steps which at first glance makes you believe you're installing the thick looking traditional looking screen protection, but you're not. If you want to avoid any mistakes read and follow the instructions carefully and I suggest spending more time on step 2 making sure all the edges and bubbles are gone. Now some little ones will be present just use the card provided and slowly move them to whatever corner is near. Over time these will dissipate on their own and the end product will leave behind some noticeable waves in the material when viewing at a angle, but nothing irritating in everyday use. Enjoy!

title: I still like Otterbox, but haven't been using it
text:
I've been using Otterbox cases since my Nokia E71, about 5 years. This was my second Otterbox for my first iPhone. I had refused to switch to iPhone until the mobile company my wife works for started carrying them on their network. I had been using HTC Androids, but didn't ever use an Otterbox with those. My first Otterbox for my iPhone was the dark blue one. I used it for about 6 months, really liked the protection and usability of it since it protected everything and every function of the phone was actually made easier to use. If I had any complaint with it, I'm just not that big on using a screen protector. I ordered this black Otterbox to replace the blue since I had gotten the blue dirty at work. I was again impressed with everything except the screen protector.

Please note, these screen protectors are the best I've seen. I've spent 30 minutes trying to put screen protectors on phones, only to run out of them. So it's really nice that these don't require any lining up. They will still get air bubbles if not careful and I really can't tell you how much I hate air bubbles on my screen.

I ended up buying another case without a screen protector. I have no doubt the screen protector serves a purpose, but barring freak accident, I'm pretty gentle with my phone. These Otterbox cases are still the best overall case if you're clumsy, if you aren't gentle with phones, they have you covered, but after getting my screen protector-less case I've also noticed how much brighter and clearer my screen is. I still have this one in its case and will keep it for any activities that may put my phone at more risk.

The magnetic part is truly the best part of the entire thing, where it definitely keeps the case closed if need be, and the part that holds the phone, holds it in tight.

So here is an accurate portrayal...
PROS...
Strong hold of your phone so it does not fall out.
Spaces to hold your cards and ID, so you do not need a purse.
Magnet holds strong.
The design on the outside of the phone cross/wings is absolutely gorgeous

CONS...
Cards/ID fall out after use
You HAVE TO USE a screen protector, or else your phone will develop a pale black streak in the screen due to the constant pressing of the black felt. THANKFULLY it has only done it to the screen protector, but if I did not have it on, my screen on my phone would be ruined.
Does not have anywhere you can actually stand it sideways on its own, as it slides.
The magnetic strip gets in the way quite frequently when trying to use your phone.

Overall, I would NOT recommend the product due to the loss of your cards and the damage it can cause to your screen of your phone. I would not chance it. The quality of the print is beautiful. When I get the money for another case, I will be going with something different.

title: Headphone slot is too small to fit the AUX IN jack for your car/home stereo; USB hole is also small.
text:
I am not satisfied with this product because the hole for the headphone jack is too small.
I plan to return this product.

This case provides good basic functionality: protect the phone and camera.
But the USB and the headphone holes are cut too small.
The USB hole makes it hard to insert.
The headphone hole is impossible to connect with audio input jack from your car/home stereo.

In a side-by-side comparison with my older Galaxy S4 case from another cheap brand,
this S6 case obviously has smaller holes.
The USB hole is cut much smaller than my S4 case, and the headphone hole is slightly smaller, but enough to be a deal breaker.

The design of a phone case should be such that you almost don't notice the case at all and can just go about your normal business.
This case fails on design.

Some of the small headphone jacks (like the one you get when you purchase a new S6) will fit fine.
But most of the serious AUX-IN jacks will not.
This prevents me from connecting my phone to my amplifier through the AUX cable.
This is the first phone case that had this problem.

All my other phone cases allow easy access to the headphone slot so I could connect my phone to my car and home stereo using a jack.
I don't always like to use Bluetooth to stream music - I think a wired connection provides better fidelity.

title: Pretty good but in no way a replacement for DSL
text:
I purchased this device like many others to be able to connect my laptop, cell phone and tablet while on the go. I've had several other big carriers including AT&T, Tmobile, verizon, and even Clearwire. I hated the fact that i needed to sign a contract and pay monthly for something that i only need to use occasionally. I also disliked the fact that 3GB was almost 50 dollars on the other providers and i would be charged for any overages at 10 dollars a gig. So i started to look elsewhere. I needed a device to have the following criteria, Decent speeds, no overages, cheap, and pre-paid for the months that i do not use it. So upon seeing this at walmart and doing further research this device seemed to fit the bill perfectly.

Initial Setup & Unboxing:

I never considered myself purchasing a prepaid cell phone or aircard for that matter, but the expensive price of overages and the low monthly caps of the larger providers forced me to look elsewhere.

The device it's small, no problems with carrying it at all in a pocket, the unit includes a replaceable battery, Micro USB cable, instructions, and a USB charger. It has a status screen for displaying usage stats, battery, signal strength and connected users etc. Initial setup is a bit tricky but not too bad. You need to connect the device via wifi ( it will show the SSID and WPA key on the device screen ) open your browser and it will connect you to the device setup page. There you will need to go to virgin mobile website enter your credit card information and choose a plan, 55 dollars for 5 Gigabytes of 3G and Unlimited 4G, or 35 dollars for 2 Gigabytes of 3G and Unlimited 4G. They will give you an account number and id which you will need to go back into the unit and enter in order to get online. I was up and running in about 20 minutes

Coverage & Speed:

I live in the city and mostly travel to other larger cities so the lack of wireless coverage outside city lines isn't a problem for me. If you live away from the cities or the outskirts for instance long island NY where there's 0 4G coverage for this device, you are pretty much stuck with the slow 3G and 2 Gigabyte Cap. To do anything in these days online, being in a 4G coverage area is an absolute must.

I travel a lot but have only had this unit for a week and haven't gotten much chance to get to too many places other than NYC and surrounding areas, But i have taken it so far to northern Jersey, Central Jersey, and all over Brooklyn and was able to keep a constant 4G signal. There are some areas that have dead spots and will pick up 3G only, but i haven't had to experience that too much. In my home in Brooklyn, i get a fairly strong 4G signal, however data speeds are pretty bad. I average anywhere from about .5 down and 1.2 up on a busy night to about 1.2 download and 1.5 upload max later in the night around 3am or so. I believe it has something to do with the towers in my area as if i drive a couple blocks away i get pretty decent speeds of 4.0 Mbps + down. This doesn't bother me too much since i have cable modem service at home and mainly use this on the go.

Certain parts of Brooklyn i was able to pick up 8-9 MBps down and 2.0 up. In Manhattan around 50th and 6th i was able to get great speeds as well, around 5.0 Down and 1-2 up. 3G was a different story, i was only able to manage about .3 down and .2 up everywhere. Not a big deal because the nice feature of this unit is you can force it to never fall back to 3G if 4G isn't available saving your 2GB bucket, or vice or versa.

One other note on signal, the 4G runs on 2.6 GHZ, a very high frequency but has the capability to carry a lot of data. It does not penetrate buildings well so this makes the signal very sensitive to weather conditions. I didn't believe this until It rained very heavy last night and i lost 4G service at home. After the rain stopped the signal returned to full bars.

Now the question is for people who are looking to replace a DSL or home line.. Can you? It boils down to two questions. How often do you use it, and how good is the coverage in your area. Id say for light usage it might be a good idea and for someone who's not on the internet 24/7. The problem is that this card gives you unlimited data but with caveats. You are only allowed full 4G speed up to 10GB and then after it is slowed to about 1.5 Mbps or so. Not too bad, but not great if you plan on streaming netflix in HD. Id say overall the device is better suited for mobile users on the go looking to do light web surfing and not a replacement for home fixed internet.

Battery Life:

Battery life is about 2-3 hours on 4G. The unit does heat up a bit, but i haven't had any problems with it shutting down or disconnecting like most people say. Maybe i have a newer revision, who knows.

Price:

At 50 dollars for the unit itself and the cheap plans, you are probably not going to get a better deal elsewhere. This unit is simply great for the price. Want to know a little secret? This unit actually uses sprints network for 3G and Clearwire's network for 4G. Clearwire charges 35 dollars for 1.5 Mbps service and 55 dollars for 4-6 Mbps service. With Virgin mobile hotspot, you are basically getting access to clear's 55 dollars service, PLUS sprints 3g for the price of clearwire's lowest tier. Ad in the fact not contracts, no overages, etc, id say its PRETTY slick deal.

Closing thoughts:

While it is not perfect and no way a replacement for a home DSL (unless you are a very light and occasional user), it is a great solution for city goers looking to access the internet. The 4G pretty much makes this device worth it, if you are not in a 4G area id say skip it, unless you really need internet access in 3G areas since it is so slow. I would have given this 5 starts if there was more 4G coverage, but i guess you cant have everything in a budget device.

title: Having signal issues but overall not a bad option; works with IPhone 3G for me as well
text:
(Note: I edited the review after I used the SIM for a while. I had initially thought it would connect to 3G but the fact that it won't is noted in the product description. Sorry about that.)

Hey folks, I ordered this SIM card in the hopes of using it at Bonnaroo, a huge music festival held near my hometown every year. Thousands of people take their AT&T IPhones to this festival, causing the cell towers to overload so badly they won't work. I've learned to bring a phone with a prepaid SIM card along for texting my friends to coordinate plans. So far this one's had its ups and downs...

* The card arrived quickly and without incident. Activating the card was fairly easy. I was able to do that online using only the card's ID number, the phone number, and my phone's serial number. However, I couldn't place calls right away because I can't get a signal on it at my house (about ten miles outside downtown Nashville, TN). It seems to work in downtown Nashville, with the Edge network on my unlocked IPhone 3G.

* I was unable to register for an online account in order to manage my minutes or find out details about my rate plan. As a condition to create the account, T-Mobile sends a text message with a temporary password to your phone and you're required to enter this password. Since I can't get a signal at all at my home, I'm unable to receive text messages. I called T-Mobile to ask to have this temporary password emailed instead (I was required to provide an email address and received an email confirming my registration of the SIM card, so I know they have my email address associated with my account.) However, the account rep insisted they don't have the ability to email me a password. I wound up grabbing the password the next time I went downtown, but it seems sort of absurd that they can't just email you the darn thing.

Upshot: This is a fairly cheap option if you need a SIM card for a one-off, like a trip to another city. I was able to get a signal pretty easily near Nashville but it didn't do so well in rural areas. Also, I couldn't get it to work either at Bonnaroo or at another 50,000 person concert in June, so don't rely on it for that purpose. But basically you can hear well using T-Mobile, it's easy to change your service plan once you're able to log into your account and I think the price tiers are fairly reasonable. I'd probably buy this again.

I thought that might be the case as the instructions to put this one reminded me of how the workers applied the UV coating to my home windows (I live in FL where the sun beats down on your house every day of the year). title: Fantastic case! VERY good value!
text:
UPDATE 10/3/16: I've been using this case for over a year now and it's still holding up very well! I'm very happy with it. It's still holding up fairly well and that's with me carrying it in my pocket most of the time. The "Leather" is showing minor signs of wear and I've not experience any issue with it pealing like some others have. I like this case a lot and the only complaint is that they don't have an extended battery cover like this. :-D

-------- Original review ---------

My phone: Verizon LG G4 with plain graphite back.

I am not often impressed with camera cases. But this one really impressed me. I ordered it expecting that "you get what you pay for", but I am completely blown away by the attention to detail of this thing. I've had it for several weeks now and I have no complaints whatsoever!

Several really nice things to note on this:

- The leather feels good. It's not too sticky. This is important for those of us who carry our phones in our pockets. You do NOT want the kind of leather that is so soft it gets stuck in your pocket or you can't pull it out because it catches on the material. Not with this cover. It's exactly the right level of stickiness. You can see the grain in pictures.

- Inside the cover there are grooves in the back of the case. At first I thought this was a just a nice design and then I realized that it's for better cooling! This was a problem I had with my last case: The phone got too hot. Not with this case! Noted in the pictures.

- The outer ring comes off. Again, at first I thought this was pointless, but the first time you put your case on, it can be a little tight. Take off the ring and the case goes right on. And as you can imagine, this works in reverse: It's harder to get the case off with the ring on it. Shown in the pictures.

These features make this case one of the nicest cases I have ever seen in this price range... and for that matter, in many levels of price range higher! I would expect if this case lasts me a year or more I'm going to be feeling like I got a steal at $17 w/Prime. If you want this kind of quality at the Verizon store you will pay at least $35 and I'm guessing this would be in their elite class at $60 or more.

VERY MUCH WORTH THE MONEY!!

title: Good idea, poorly executed
text:
I got this product for my hybrid bicycle, which I ride for pleasure on weekends, riding 10-20 miles on average. The main reason I chose this product over others is because of the ability to easily detach the phone for usage, without taking it out of of the mount. The issue is that the way this mount is made, while it's study and the phone probably won't fall out, makes the phone constantly rattle when riding over even just slightly uneven surfaces. And the worse the ground surface, the worse and the louder the rattling noise gets. The noise is quite annoying and when I am riding nearby other bikers, I noticed others looking at me and my bike because the noise is that loud and irritating that others can clearly hear it.
Btw, this rattling noise happens regardless of how well and tightly the mount is connected to the handlebars.
I haven't decided whether I will keep or return it yet, because I am waiting to see if other buyers or the seller will answer the question I asked about whether this is a fixable issue.
Lastly, I also think it's a bit overpriced for what it is, and esp given this design flaw. For what it is, it should be no more than $10-12.

title: Is your phone water proof?
text:
Is your phone water proof? Mine neither, but we swim with this all the time and it still survives.
The pros-
You can use your phone in and around water without worrying about damage. That's what it's made for, and it works.
Shooting video under water works, as long as you get it rolling before you dunk it.
The cons-
It is not easy to use the touch screen underwater, I've tried with a few different phones and it doesn't work on any of them. And because of the shape, it is too difficult to access the camera button that one of my phones (Lumia 930) on the bezel. So good luck taking any pictures under water.
It would be hard to say that it looks good. It's bulky and cheesy looking. And pictures look okay through it, but not great.
Final thoughts. It's great for a trip to the pool or beach if you're not interested in underwater photography.

title: Nice case, but lacks screen protection
text:
The case itself appears to be nice and durable. The raised bumpers on the top and bottom of the phone are higher than expected, and that's a good thing, but the sides are not raised enough for peace of mind. The case itself fits great, once you manage to get it on. It was a bit difficult to snap in, and this being my first smartphone, I was worried I was going to snap the phone trying to wedge it in, which obviously I was wrong. The description says it fits with Alpha Glass, but I have serious doubts about being able to get this case on without destroying whatever screen protector gets applied. And if they recommend Alpha Glass, why can't they just include it all in one nice little package? Smh.

All in all, this is a nice durable case, but without screen protection, it's inevitable that things will go wrong one day.
I'm off to purchase the Alpha Glass, after skimming though the reviews. Maybe.

EDIT: 10/06/18
After using it for about a week, and taking it off, I found out that it's much easier to remove and put back on, in pieces. Much easier, duh.
I couldn't find "Alpha Glass", so I ended up purchasing a OTAO Tempered Glass screen https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B074SJV133/ref=oh_aui_detailpage_o00_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1, and it does fit the S8, NOT 100%, but I have a feeling with this curved screen, perfection is not an option. The jury is still out on the effectiveness of the OTAO, since I was able to slide it off without realizing.

EDIT: 12/02/2021
I've had this case on for over 3 years now. I gave up on the additional tempered glass; couldn't find one that would stay on to my liking. In June 2021, the original Otterbox plastic skeleton had broken, so I ordered another case (the blue one) just for the skeleton and will use the blue case as a backup. I could have purchased just the skeleton on eBay but for a few more bucks, I'd have an actual Otterbox product. I have dropped my phone MANY times over these 3 years, and have never broken the screen. This case has been awesome.

text: I have had a Motorola Moto G6 phone since 2019, and recently it began expanding like a clamshell pushing the back panel open. It comes with a box of tools including 5 little screwdrivers, two peel and stick pads, and three other little tools I don't have names for.  The complexity of it all didn't look promising.  I didn't watch the manufacturer's YouTube videos on how to install the battery but just took everything back to the repair shop, concluding it would be cheaper, faster and less stressful to pay them to install the battery with all this stuff than for me to try it, ruin my phone, and have to buy a new one.  The install cost $40.  It was worth it, and the phone no longer bulges and works just fine.

title: Does not work with screen protector! Ruined my screen protector!!
text:
I really wanted to love this band/case and was super excited to receive it! I have a collection of 9 or 10 different GShocks ...that was all i wore before I started getting more into cycling/fitness and I am fairly new to the fitness tracker world! I run an auto detailing business so I am constantly banging my hands and wrist on stuff while cleaning vehicles! So i thought this band would be a perfect fit for me to help keep my ionic nice and safe while scrubbing carpets under seats and banging it on anything and everything inside vehicles! It is more at home with the bigger beefier look of the gshock watches I normally wear! The look of the Supcase band is decent the "carbon fiber" style look on the sides is not nearly as noticeable in person as it looks in the pictures.The material is a decent feeling material, its halfway comfortable but not nearly as soft and comfy as the factory band on my adidas ionic, nor is it as soft as the silicon on the other "two tone" bands you can buy on here for cheap! The band on the supcase feels almost like a hard foam material! The biggest problem I had with the fit was I couldnt find a perfect size on the band for my medium sized wrist! The 3rd set of holes was too tight as the 4th set of holes was a tad too loose...I do not have tiny wrist either so I could see this being pretty big for most people! Overall I did like the look and decent comfort of the band and would have kept it based off these alone! BUT...........

Here is where i have the biggest problem with the Supcase for fitbit Ionic and the reason I am only leaving 2 stars! The case/cover/band whatever you want to call it does not have a screen protector! As anything I spend this much money on I am going to put a screen protector on it! The problem is it DOES NOT work with screen protectors! In fact, it actually completely destroyed my screen protector making me need to purchase a new one! Which is terrible because I spent 15 dollars (out of my own stupidity) at Best B on the screen protector when i purchased my ionic! So now im out another 7 or 8 dollars because of the supcase band! When I first got it i opened it up out of excitement took my other band off and slapped my ionic inside this case then flipped it over to see that the case had completely tore off the bottom left corner of my screen protector! So I took it back out, fixed my screen protector and very carefully tried sticking the ionic back in my case as soft and carefull as possible to not tear up my screen protector again! I lined it up perfectly and got the watch in with out tearing up the corners this time! All is good, right?.....So i wore the supcase for the last couple hours of the day, no problems kept my ionic nice and safe! Went to bed with my ionic on and woke up to my screen protector Completely destroyed from this band! Its really too bad because I really wanted this case for my ionic as its by far the best option when looking for something to completely protect your expensive fitness tracker, especially if you work with your hands all day like I do! Also it would be really nice if they would offer this band in more colors then just black! Unfortunatly I returned this band and will most likely just pay the 60 dollars for the protection plan on my ionic and not worry so much about getting it banged up or scratched as I know I will be able to replace it in the future with the protection plan

title: Perfect fit and color matches phone but ...
text:
This case is the perfect fit and the yellow color matches my yellow Lumia 1520 however it does 'turn' a blue-grayish color where the push buttons are from use. I have not been able to clean off the discoloration but it is only on the side where the push buttons are. I feel it protects my phone. I think the camera cut-out is just barely raised enough that it does protect the lens. I have read a lot of reviews that indicate it does not but I think it does. I have this exact case in each color it comes in. With the PINK case on, I can see the camera lens cut-out appears to be just slightly raised above the phone camera lens - it is difficult to tell when I have yellow on yellow. This case is very tight fitting and I took the advice of another reviewer and was cautious not to push on the front glass screen when putting the case on as to not crack my glass screen. I have found it easier to put the case on side to side rather than top to bottom. This case keeps the phone looking slim and I can still easily slide in and out of a (larger) pocket. I would purchase again.

COLORS FYI - I purchased all colors available for the 1520. The yellow is a perfect match. Although I like the purple, pink and blue, they are ALL DARKER than they appear on the screen. They appear to be light colored. Purple is a deep purple. Pink is dark, not a barbie pink. The blue is very dark blue however not navy. Hope this helps. I was slightly disappointed as I purchased due to color they appear to be on screen. Of course the black is a normal black.
